review_scope_note: Full-repository audit. The signing reviewer recomputed the regression from the raw committed logs, verified all five SHA-256 digests, and recomputed the secondary tables from the all-subsets CSV.
verification_methods: Re-ran the 5-point OLS: 31.5 + 4.47*log10(N), R^2 = 0.9984, residuals [-0.32, +0.36, +0.38, +0.12, -0.53] — every statistic matches the frontmatter exactly, including all five residuals
Verified all five claimed SHA-256 prefixes (14c69b3c0885, ecc0c96d5817, 68a9512d8147, bd5e57d5ef20, 5115d64d8c6b) against the committed log files — all match
Recomputed the digit-1 sigmoid table (avg density with/without digit 1 at each cardinality) from density_all_subsets_n10_1e6.csv — all 14 values match to the printed precision

Recomputed the {1,2,k} exception counts at 10^6 from the CSV (27, 64, 373, 1720, 5388, 11746, 21796, 33025 — exact) and re-fit the log-log exponent: 6.42, R^2 = 0.986 (my 95% CI [5.65, 7.19] vs the published [5.80, 7.04] — same point estimate, slightly different CI convention)
Confirmed gpu_A12_1e13.log and gpu_A12_1e14.log exist, consistent with the page's disclosure that they record out-of-memory failures, not results

claim_reviews.claim: The five densities are empirical GPU measurements: 57.98 / 72.06 / 76.55 / 80.75 / 84.58 (%) at N = 10^6..10^12.
claim_reviews.evidence: All five parsed from the committed logs with matching SHA-256 digests. Nothing extrapolated is presented as measured.

claim_reviews.claim: 5-point fit: density = 31.5 + 4.47*log10(N), R^2 = 0.9984, residuals [-0.32, 0.36, 0.38, 0.12, -0.53]; the -0.53 residual at 10^12 may signal sub-logarithmic curvature.
claim_reviews.evidence: Reviewer's own OLS reproduces every quoted statistic exactly, including all five residuals to two decimals. The interpretation — largest residual at the newest point, treated as possible curvature onset rather than confirmation of the model — is statistically honest.

sources.reference: Reviewer OLS on the five log-parsed densities

claim_reviews.claim: Predictions (89.6% at 10^13, 98.5% at 10^15, 100% near 10^15.3) are extrapolations; 10^13/10^14 attempts OOM-failed; five points make a fit, not a proof.
claim_reviews.evidence: Every prediction is explicitly labeled an extrapolation, the OOM failures are disclosed rather than hidden, and the closing caveat is unambiguous. The distinction drawn between R(d) growth (exponent 2*delta-1 = 0.062) and density convergence — with the explicit statement that no rigorous bridge is established — is exactly the right epistemic posture.

claim_reviews.claim: Digit-1 sigmoid (advantage peaks at cardinality 4: 92.1% vs 12.7%) and {1,2,k} exception scaling ~ 0.02*k^6.4 (R^2 = 0.986).
claim_reviews.evidence: Both tables recompute exactly from the committed all-subsets CSV; the reviewer's independent OLS gives slope 6.42 and R^2 0.986. Minor: my 95% CI is [5.65, 7.19], slightly wider than the published [5.80, 7.04] — likely a different SE convention; the point estimate and fit quality are identical.
claim_reviews.concerns: State the CI convention (t-quantile and df) for the 6.42 exponent.

overall_assessment: This finding is fully reproducible from committed artifacts down to the second decimal of each regression residual, with correct SHA-256 digests for all five inputs, honest labeling of every extrapolation, and disclosure of the failed 10^13/10^14 attempts. The R(d)-vs-density distinction in the summary preempts the most tempting overclaim. Together with the digit-pair page, this is the project's evidentiary gold standard even though certification policy caps it lower.
recommendations: Document the CI convention for the k^6.42 exponent
certification_justification: Every measured number, both regressions, all hashes, and both secondary tables verified independently; predictions cleanly separated from measurements. Silver is fully earned.
